# Public source extraction

The repository contains numeric source facts, source locators and executable extraction logic. It does not contain source PDFs, figure rasters or copied article prose. Source access and reuse terms are recorded per artifact; no source is admitted here for model-weight training. Numerical facts do not imply a license to redistribute the original expression.

## Files and reproduction

- `../src/ndfeb_sps/models/data/density.csv`: 38 uniquely identified rows, including interval, lower-bound and conflicted observations. `default_fit` selects 33 rows in seven separate recipe slices.
- `../src/ndfeb_sps/models/data/sources.json`: source identity, rights status, route limits and warnings.
- `../src/ndfeb_sps/models/data/wu2025.json`: separate prospective source facts, stage/population definitions, conflicts and missing quantities from the final Wu paper; no new fitted rows.
- `extraction_receipt.json`: extraction locators, source/raster hashes, pixel calibration and exclusions.
- `replay_results.json`: executed source reconstruction and internal leave-one-temperature-out diagnostics. This is not independent validation.
- `digitize_mishra.py`: reproducible marker extraction from the original 1880 × 1387 JPEG embedded on PDF page 6. It writes JSON to stdout only. Pillow is an optional extraction-time dependency, not a forecast dependency.

The public Mishra PDF and inspected rasters are kept outside this repository under the sibling `ndfeb-sps-campaign-artifacts/sources/` directory. With a locally accessed source PDF, extract the original JPEG using `pdfimages -f 6 -l 6 -j`, then pass the first page-6 JPEG to `digitize_mishra.py`. Image scaling or screenshot compression changes the pixel coordinate system and must not be silently substituted. The inspected raster SHA-256 is in the receipt.

From this repository, replay the supported model with:

```sh
PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python -c 'import json; from ndfeb_sps.models import source_replay_report; print(json.dumps(source_replay_report(), indent=2))'
PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_models.py tests/test_source_v2.py -q
```

The extraction script was also executed against the external original raster and reproduced all four receipt values and the raster checksum. If Pillow is absent from the campaign runtime, an isolated extraction environment avoids changing that runtime:

```sh
uv run --no-project --with numpy --with pillow python sources/digitize_mishra.py ../ndfeb-sps-campaign-artifacts/sources/mishra_page6-000.jpg
```

## Source-specific evidence and limitations

### Mishra et al., 2023

[Article](https://doi.org/10.1002/adem.202201027), [public PDF](https://d-nb.info/1269737651/34). The PDF states CC BY-NC-ND. Independently extracted numerical facts only are included here; no derivative figure or article is redistributed.

Methods 2.2 describes non-field-aligned FAST/SPS of commercial MQU-F powder, lot B55557: 15 g, 20 mm die, 50 MPa, 100 °C/min and 30 s hold. Figure 4a on PDF page 6 supplies the density-versus-temperature markers. Figure 2c illustrates why total punch displacement cannot be treated as pure irreversible specimen shrinkage.

The digitized relative densities at 500/600/700/800 °C are approximately 79.8/91.8/98.4/98.4%. Conversion uses the source reference density, 7.63 g/cm³. Decimal arithmetic in the derived densities is not additional measurement precision. The figure's 500 °C point conflicts with the Methods 2.2 interval of 73–75%; both observations remain visible and 500 °C is excluded from the baseline. Raw manufacturing replicate counts and physical measurement SD are unknown. A grain-image temperature conflict also prevents extracting a portable quantitative grain-growth relation.

### Keszler et al., 2025

[Article](https://doi.org/10.1177/00325899251331431), [public author-repository PDF](https://juser.fz-juelich.de/record/1052723/files/keszler-et-al-2025-field-assisted-sintering-and-spark-plasma-texturing-of-nd-fe-b-magnets-with-anisotropic-magnetic.pdf). Public access was verified; exact reuse terms were not independently resolved. Only numerical facts are included.

The pre-hot-deformation MQU-F observations provide an important route comparison, not a pooled calibration set. Methods/Figure 3, Table 3 and Figure 8 use different geometry and process settings across conditions. Retained density observations are 70–75% at 500 °C, approximately 90% at 700 °C, and greater than 99% at 725 °C; the source reference density is 7.55 g/cm³. The 700/725 °C series uses 5 g/10 mm geometry, 75 °C/min and 60 s, unlike the Mishra slice. Reported pressure is inconsistent among 45, 48 and 50 MPa; it remains null in the source point rows. A lower bound is never fitted as an exact value. Later hot-deformation magnetic results are excluded. These rows are not a matched holdout.

### Ikram et al., 2019

[Article](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jallcom.2018.09.322). The first page states CC BY 4.0. Table 2 on journal page 1202 was re-inspected against the existing public-source artifact.

The 30 density entries cover six separate temperature slices: three ramp/hold choices, each before and after annealing. There are 15 paired preparation histories, not 30 independent manufacturing repeats. All belong to recycled HDDR powder, 5 g/16 mm and 50 MPa. They remain a separate `recycled_hddr_sps` branch; neither melt-spun MQU-F nor aligned HPMS is pooled with them. The table-specific ramp labels are retained despite a methods/table mismatch. Grain descriptors on journal page 1200 are retained as source observations; their reported plus-minus quantities are not predictive uncertainty.

## Additional access that would materially help

1. **Wu, Zhao, Cui and Lian (2025), underlying data and any supplements**, DOI [10.1016/j.jallcom.2025.183663](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jallcom.2025.183663); preprint DOI [10.2139/ssrn.5205331](https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.5205331). The final paper was unavailable for the frozen initial source packet but was subsequently obtained and fully reviewed. No abstract-only row entered the fit, and the completed investigator runs were not given this new evidence. The article adds useful pre-hot-deformation observations; missing raw histories, measurement definitions and source conflicts still limit calibration. See the full-text update below. A named publication instrument does not establish the current RPI installation or access.
2. **Song et al. (2026)**, DOI [10.1016/j.jallcom.2026.187915](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jallcom.2026.187915). The full text was not retrieved despite the public page indicating open access. The reported initial-grain-heterogeneity explanation is a useful competitor to thermal-contact explanations. Needed: full methods, pre/post grain distributions and density series. No numeric calibration is taken from an abstract alone.

For all three extracted studies, author-supplied specimen-level data and clarification of conflicting settings would be more valuable for uncertainty estimation than extracting further decimal places from a plotted mean.

## Full-text update: Wu et al. (2025)

The eight-page final paper was read completely, including visual inspection of all ten figures and both tables, with four independent subject-specific reviews. Its PDF SHA-256 is `82955f863d7f20b00f3f726a885480e62aad5f84fd38a6a6b182a69155846632`. The PDF and review rasters remain outside this repository. The article carries an Elsevier all-rights-reserved notice; no redistribution or model-weight training admission follows from access.

Figure 3E (page 4) prints these **initial-SPS, fine-region** observations:

| Figure temperature | Pressure from caption | Relative density | Fine-region grain size |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 350 °C | 300 MPa | 91% TD | 50.1 nm |
| 450 °C | 200 MPa | 98% TD | 51.8 nm |
| 550 °C; related text/Figure 2 says 500 °C | 50 MPa | 95% TD | 82.9 nm |
| 650 °C | 50 MPa | 99% TD | 130.1 nm |

These are printed labels, not a new pixel-digitized fit. The middle condition remains conflict-marked; it is not silently corrected. No theoretical-density denominator is supplied, so the percentages are not converted to g/cm³ using another source's reference. Grain error-bar meaning and manufacturing replication are unknown.

The approximately 4 g MQU-F charges use 100 °C/min heating but an unquantified hold until displacement becomes steady. Tooling changes from 8 mm graphite below 60 MPa to 10 mm tungsten carbide above 60 MPa. Pressure, tooling and actual dwell therefore prevent treating these as a matched temperature-only calibration. They do not identify pressure sensitivity, grain-growth kinetics or predictive noise. Fine-region size is not whole-specimen grain size or powder PSD.

Later hot-deformation results belong to different physical histories. In particular, the reported 48 MGOe result follows 350 °C/300 MPa initial SPS and subsequent 710 °C hot deformation; it is not the magnetic performance of an SPS-only compact. Figure-local A–D labels cannot be joined across stages, and the 650 °C/40 MPa hot-deformation precursor differs from Figure 3's 650 °C/50 MPa point. No post-deformation anneal is reported.

The initial full-text review changed source-access documentation only; no completed investigator run received these facts. The subsequent **prospective v2** source packet now includes the reviewed numerical facts and short factual summaries in `wu2025.json`, without article prose, rasters or the PDF. No redistribution or model-weight training permission for the source document is asserted.

`source_observations("wu_2025", stage="initial_sps")` returns the four initial observations; `include_conflicted=False` removes the ambiguous middle point. Separate `post_hot_deformation` and `post_hot_deformation_thermal` records retain Tables 1/2 and Figure 10B, without converting HD platelet widths or magnetic performance to SPS-only outcomes. `source_applicability(...)` describes the source and measurement correspondence and returns no fitted Wu prediction. Unknown dwell, denominator, powder-lot identity, measurement counts and additional-treatment history remain unknown.

The 38 CSV rows, 33 fitted points, seven original recipe slices and saved source-replay values remain unchanged. Existing historical source packets, investigator models, forecasts and outcomes are not rewritten. The new source packet is explicitly versioned `ndfeb-public-sources-v2`; the forecast's limited applicability-matching correction is documented in `docs/CALIBRATION.md`, separately from agent-authored learning. Highest-value remaining source gaps are the 500/550 °C clarification, per-specimen SPS/density/microscopy records, actual dwell times, theoretical-density basis, starting-lot history and uncertainty definitions.
